meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas (live data, not an archived version; give corpus_snapshot and source_commit). doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Ras-MAPK growth signalling converges on the same brake that Akt releases, through two kinases: ERK phosphorylates TSC2 (MA2005) and RSK1 binds tuberin and phosphorylates Ser-1798 at its conserved C terminus (ROU2004). Either phosphorylation inactivates the TSC complex. This is the third upstream arm alongside PI3K/Akt and AMPK, and clinically it is a route to mTORC1 activation that PI3K inhibitors do not close.
data.mechanism_beginner: A separate growth pathway also disables the TSC brake – a third route into mTORC1 that drugs blocking only PI3K/Akt can't shut down.
data.context: The source node groups ERK and RSK, and both arms are now held in this corpus: MA2005 for ERK phosphorylating TSC2, ROU2004 for RSK1 phosphorylating tuberin at Ser-1798. Both were measured in mammalian cell lines, and neither study establishes which of the two kinases carries the signal in a given cell type or tissue.
data.boundary: Two studies in mammalian cell lines, one for each kinase in the grouped source node: ERK to TSC2 (MA2005) and RSK1 to TSC2 Ser-1798 (ROU2004). Neither was tested in whole animals or in people, and neither measures the relative weight of the two arms.
data.note: Added 2026-07-29. The graph previously had no MAPK input to mTORC1 at all.
